# The Stone Warren
## *the night the floor came up at Brackenmouth*

A one-night adventure for three to five Fell at level 1, on [[The FellGuide/The FellGuide/The Lore (Contains Spoilers)/The Sphere/Stratums/Shervinaw|Shervinaw]]. It is a rescue against a clock. The Fell are the biggest things in a warren full of frightened, stubborn, knee-high people, and the night asks them to be useful. Plan on about three and a half hours.

Everything you need is in this folder. The scenes run in the order the Fell choose after the second one. Each opens with what you read aloud. The foes' numbers are on their own pages.

## Before you run it

- Hold the talk from [[The Fell Who Forgot]] with each player before the night. The Fell wake with no memory, and the first scene hands out a Lore Drop on a Fellmark, so have one ready for each Fell.
- Every Fell wakes on Shervinaw as the adventure's world, so each one holds Rootsummons at competency 0, the magic of calling the living wood to grow, hold or bend. Tell the players. It works on the grey root tonight, and it is one of the ways through more than one scene. A Rootsummons roll is 1d6 + its competency, so 1d6 + 0 tonight, against your 1d6 + 0. A Fellmark raises it by 1 like any skill.
- Skill Difficulty is +0. You roll 1d6 + 0 against every skill check. Your lever is Luck, as [[Making the Call]] sets it out.
- Draw the floor clock on paper where the whole table can see it: a circle cut into four. Draw ten small rafts next to it and cross each one off as it leaves.
- Read the three foe pages.

## What is really going on

Shervinaw is a world of giant trees, and the Shrewish live in the roots. They are a small, whiskered people, about knee height to most Fell, and their children are the size of ordinary rats. They build, they plan, and they hoard food against bad years, because the roots taught them that bad years come. Their warrens are tunnels in living roots, and the roots open and close them.

For three years a grey rot, the blight, has spread through those roots. A blighted root goes soft and grey, closes its tunnels on whoever is inside, and grows over anything warm. The Slumpwood, a forest upriver, went grey this spring, and its people fled.

They fled to [[Brackenmouth]]. It is the one warren on Shervinaw dug into riverbank clay and walled with stone, because a root cannot close stone. Two hundred Shrewish are crowded into it tonight with everything they could carry.

[[Nib Sorrelgate]] built Brackenmouth. Last spring she dug a shaft under its lower tunnels, looking for clean water, and broke into a hollow where a mother root nobody had mapped ran through the clay. It was already grey. She plugged the shaft with clay instead of stone, because stone would have taken until summer, and she told nobody. Tonight the root has broken through her clay plug and is growing up the shaft toward the warmest place in the riverbank, which is two hundred frightened people.

Nobody here is a villain. The root has no mind. It grows. Nib made one bad call and has been sick about it since. The danger is the root, and the people's own stubbornness about leaving.

## How the Fell win

There are two ways to win, and the best night does both.

- **Get them out.** The Sallowrun is the slow brown river below the warren. It is the one road on Shervinaw the roots cannot close. Ten rafts at the river door each carry twenty Shrewish.
- **Seal the root.** Down Nib's shaft, at the bottom, the Fell set stone across the shaft mouth while the root fights back. Sealed, the root is cut off and Brackenmouth stands.

## The three things you track

Read this section before the night. Every scene that uses one of these says so again where it comes up.

> [!reminder] The floor clock
> **What it is.** How far the grey root has grown up under Brackenmouth. Draw a circle on paper, cut it into four, and put it where the whole table can see it.
>
> **How it moves.** After scene 2, at the end of every scene, look at where the Fell are. If no Fell is at the shaft, fill one segment. If at least one Fell is at the shaft, it does not move. "At the shaft" means anywhere from the hole at the top of the shaft down to the hollow at the bottom. The clock also fills one segment whenever a Fell at the shaft rolls a Fellstrike, because the noise and the shaking wake the root. Nothing else moves it.
>
> **What each segment means.** Read it out when it fills, and show it as a sound first.
> 1. The lower tunnels crack, and grey bark shows in the floor.
> 2. The larders split open, and soft grey wood comes up through the food. Anyone still in the larders runs for the river door.
> 3. The floor of the great hall splits down the middle.
> 4. The root reaches the river door. The last raft must go now. From here the shaft can't be sealed, only held.
>
> **Why it matters.** It decides how much stone the Fell need, and whether sealing the shaft is still possible.

> [!reminder] Stone needed
> **What it is.** How many loads of stone it takes to wall off the shaft at the bottom.
>
> **How to work it out.** 2, plus the segments filled on the floor clock when the Fell reach the bottom of the shaft. Arrive at once and it takes 2. Arrive after two segments and it takes 4.
>
> **Why it matters.** It is the cost of going to the river first. Waiting never hurts anyone. It means more stone to set in the fight.

> [!reminder] The rafts
> **What they are.** Ten rafts at the river door, twenty Shrewish to a raft. Two hundred people.
>
> **How they get away.** Scene 4 is about getting the loading running. Once it runs, Dobb and his crew keep it going on their own, and every raft is away before the root reaches the river door. You don't count rafts scene by scene. Cross them off as you like for the table to see, and settle who got away at the end, by the rule below.
>
> **Who is left on the quay at the end.** Nobody, if the Fell sealed the shaft (no one needed to leave) or held the root at the bottom until the last raft went (holding buys Dobb the time to load everyone). If they did neither:
> - eighty Shrewish are left if the loading never got running, because Dobb alone gets only six rafts away.
> - twenty more are left if Furze's food rode on the rafts and nobody made room for it.
>
> **Why it matters.** It decides between the Emptied ending and The Last Raft.

## The choices that shape the night

These are the choices the Fell make that change a later scene. Each scene tells you when to write one down. Here is the whole map, so nothing surprises you.

| The choice | Made in | The answers | What it changes later |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Where the Fell start | [[02 - Nib\|Nib]] | The river door, the shaft, or both at once | The order you run scenes 3 to 6, and how far the clock has moved when they reach the shaft. |
| Did Furze come out of his larder? | [[03 - The Larders\|The Larders]] | He came, or he stayed | If he stayed, sixty Shrewish stay with him until the clock's second segment, then come running. He speaks to the Fell at dawn only if they talked him out. |
| Did the food come too? | The Larders | It came, it came and the Fell made room, or it stayed | If it came and nobody made room, twenty more are left on the quay if the shaft is neither sealed nor held. |
| Is the loading running at the river door? | [[04 - The River Door\|The River Door]] | Running, or not | Who is left on the quay if the shaft is neither sealed nor held. See The rafts. |
| Did Dobb hold his nerve? | The River Door | He held, or he froze | What he says at dawn. |
| How did the shaft end? | [[06 - The Grey Mother\|The Grey Mother]] | Sealed, held until the last raft, or every Fell fell | Which ending you read. |
| Nib's secret | [[07 - Nib's Secret\|Nib's Secret]] | Told, or kept | One read-aloud in the ending, and what Nib does next. |

## The night and the river

The adventure runs from full dark to first light, one night in late spring. It is warm and close underground, and the air smells of clay, river water and pickled roots. The river is high and fast but safe on a raft. A Fell who goes in can climb out or be pulled out. Water deals no damage here and calls for no roll unless a scene says so.

Show the floor clock whenever the Fell move somewhere new. Every segment is a sound first: a crack, a groan in the stone, the hum under everyone's feet getting louder.

The Shrewish act like Shrewish. Every family has a plan, a pack and a list. None of the plans agree. They do not panic for long, and they argue about everything.

## Who the Fell are

People in Brackenmouth react to some Fell on sight. Each scene carries the lines for these. Play every other lineage as big, strange and useful. The Shrewish have no time to be afraid of anyone tonight, and they size each Fell up for how much it can carry.

- **A Shrewish Fell** is one of their own, a cousin from some other warren. They are told everything first and handed the heaviest job anyway. [[Old Furze]] listens to a Shrewish before anyone else. Nib looks them in the eye and lies anyway, and it costs her more. A Shrewish Fell stands at the same knee height as everyone else here and fits the shaft with room to spare.
- **A Fell with a Felionis** gets room. The [[The Felionis|Felionis]] is Shervinaw's own lorebound, a bark-plated hunting cat grown from the mother roots, and the Shrewish fall quiet around it. The [[The Flat-Eyed Felionis|flat-eyed Felionis]] in the shaft goes for someone else first. That is story, and it changes no number.

## What the foes want

None of the foes in this adventure is evil, and none of them hates the Fell.

- **The Grey Mother** is the growing tip of a rotten root. It has no mind and wants one thing, warmth. It grows toward the warmest thing near it, and tonight that is two hundred people packed into a riverbank. It cannot be talked to or frightened. It can be walled off with stone.
- **The rootbound weasels** are weasels the root caught and wound in bark. Nothing is left of them. The root moves them the way you move your fingers, and they go where it reaches, toward warmth: lamps, fires, bodies. They have no fear and no anger. They can be got past without a fight. Put the lamps out and stand still and they lose you, or set a lit lamp down a side tunnel and they follow it. They are fought only when the Fell need to work by lamplight where they are, which at the bottom of the shaft they do.
- **The flat-eyed Felionis** is a guard. A Felionis guards the new shoots of the forest the way a dog guards a yard, and this one went into the grey and came back guarding the root instead. It is not hungry and it is not cruel. It goes for whoever threatens what it guards, which means whoever is setting stone. It can be stopped without a fight: a Fell can reach the old guard under the grey with Rootsummons and turn it, or a Fell with a Felionis can stand it down. Scene 6 says how.

## When a roll goes badly

A Fellstrike already goes wrong, and a Failure already costs the Fell what they reached for. The results in this adventure stop there. None of them makes a later roll Unlucky, deals damage, takes something away or adds a foe. The floor clock is the night's cost, and it moves only as written above. If you want a bad roll to follow the Fell into the story, that is your call at the table, and the game gives you the tools:

- Luck is your lever. You may make any later roll Unlucky, theirs or yours, as [[Making the Call]] sets it out.
- Hard work may cost a rank of Fatigue on a failed Endurance check. Hauling stone all night is hard work. Call it rarely.
- Noise can bring more company. One more [[Rootbound Weasel]] can come out of the walls in either fight.
- A Fellstrike makes the wrong thing happen. Choose what that is from the scene in front of you.

## Every route

| Route | Scenes | What it gives and costs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| River first | 3, 4, then 5, 6 | Every raft is loading before they go down. The floor clock stands at 2 when they reach the shaft, so they need 4 loads of stone. |
| Shaft first | 5, 6 | A gamble that usually pays. A seal at clock 0 needs 2 loads, and once it is sealed nobody has to leave. If Fellstrikes in the shaft push the clock to 4 first, the Fell can only hold the root, and the river door has had nobody working it. Holding still buys Dobb the time to get everyone out. |
| Split | Both at once | The usual choice. The shaft team fights shorter-handed, the river team gets the loading running, and the clock does not move while anyone is at the shaft. |

Every route ends with [[07 - Nib's Secret|Nib's Secret]] and [[08 - Dawn on the Sallowrun|Dawn on the Sallowrun]]. If every Fell falls in the shaft, skip scene 7 and read the Defeat ending.

The Fell can split up, and most tables will. Run the two groups a scene at a time, back and forth. Each scene says who it is for and where everyone is at the end of it.

## How the night ends

The question the night answers is this: **do two hundred Shrewish get through the night, and does Brackenmouth stand?** Every ending says the answer out loud, then closes on a read-aloud. Choose the ending in scene 8 like this.

| What happened at the shaft | Who was left on the quay | The ending | The answer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sealed | Nobody | **The Stone Holds** | Everyone lives, and Brackenmouth stands. Anyone already downriver comes back by noon. The root is walled off for good. |
| Held until the last raft | Nobody | **Emptied** | Everyone lives, and Brackenmouth is lost to the root. They go downriver to Quillbark Hold with what they carried. |
| Neither sealed nor held, and nobody left by the rule in The rafts | Nobody | **Emptied** | As above. |
| Neither sealed nor held | Twenty, eighty or a hundred, by the rule in The rafts | **The Last Raft** | Most live. The ones left on the quay are named. Brackenmouth is lost. |
| Every Fell fell | By the rule in The rafts | **Defeat** | Nib drags the Fell out. Everyone on the rafts lives, and anyone left on the quay is named. Brackenmouth is lost. |

## If the Fell go off the page

- **They leave Brackenmouth on the first raft.** Let them. The raft goes downriver and the warren's lamps go small behind them. Dobb will not push off until the raft is full, so they wait at the quay long enough to hear the floor groan behind them. Give them the choice again there.
- **They try to dig a new way out.** The Shrewish think it is a fine idea and hand them shovels. It takes all night. Treat it as working the river door. The clock moves the same as when no one is at the shaft.
- **They try to burn the root.** Fire works on the grey wood the way it works on wet bread. It smokes, it stinks and it barely catches. A burning root makes the shaft fight harder to breathe in, and that is all.
- **They turn on Nib.** She does not fight. She tells them where the stone is anyway.
- **A Fell falls to Pandemonium.** Run [[Running Pandemonium]] as written.
- **The whole table loses at the bottom of the shaft.** Read the Defeat ending.

## The numbers for this night

Built from [[Building Crucibles]] at an Average Party Level of 1. A Minion is worth half a Fell, an Elite one Fell and a Champion a Fell and a half. Disruptions are your pool for making a fight harder in the moment, as Building Crucibles sets out: the number of Fell + 1 for each battle. Close every battle in canon's order: name the defeated, the Fatigue check, the Treasure Phase, then Lore Points. A foe the Fell get past by a roll instead of a fight counts as defeated, and pays its Lore Points. Down the Shaft pays 1. The Grey Mother pays 6 if the shaft is sealed, and 3 if it is only held. A table that seals the shaft earns 7 in all, and a table that holds it earns 4.
